selected_trials.title: ROSEWOOD: A Phase II Randomized Study of Zanubrutinib Plus Obinutuzumab Versus Obinutuzumab Monotherapy in Patients With Relapsed or Refractory Follicular Lymphoma
selected_trials.population: 217 adults with grade 1–3a follicular lymphoma after at least two prior systemic lines, including anti-CD20 antibody and alkylating-agent exposure; 145 assigned to zanubrutinib plus obinutuzumab and 72 to obinutuzumab.
selected_trials.intervention: Zanubrutinib 160 mg orally twice daily with obinutuzumab 1,000 mg IV on the protocol schedule; zanubrutinib continued until progression or unacceptable toxicity. Exact obinutuzumab maintenance schedule requires protocol-level recheck.
selected_trials.comparator: Obinutuzumab 1,000 mg IV on the same protocol schedule without zanubrutinib.
selected_trials.endpoint: Overall response rate by independent central review.
selected_trials.follow: Primary JCO report; median follow-up approximately 20 months. Long-term OS maturity and full follow-up table extraction remain open.
selected_trials.efficacy: ORR 69% versus 46% (p=0.0012); complete response 39% versus 19%. Median PFS was approximately 28.0 versus 10.4 months (HR 0.50, 95% CI 0.33–0.75). These are primary-report estimates; the complete time-to-event table and data cutoff require final table-level reconciliation.
selected_trials.safety: Grade ≥3 toxicity, serious adverse events, dose interruptions, infections, cytopenias, bleeding and treatment discontinuations require full primary-table/supplement extraction before release. Do not infer missing rates.
selected_trials.qol: No patient-reported quality-of-life result has been verified from the primary report in this run.
selected_trials.burden: Continuous oral BTK inhibition plus protocol-scheduled IV anti-CD20 therapy versus IV anti-CD20 alone; exact dose intensity, interruptions and discontinuations remain to be reconciled.
selected_trials.limitations: Phase II, open-label, modest sample size and 2:1 randomization. ORR is assessed at a study cutoff rather than a fixed landmark, so no NNT is calculated. Full grade 3–5 safety tables and protocol schedule remain open.
selected_trials.interpretation: The randomized signal supports activity of adding zanubrutinib to obinutuzumab in heavily pretreated follicular lymphoma, but this page remains a draft until dose schedule, full safety tables and follow-up maturity are checked directly against the article and supplement.

selected_trials.title: Tumor Treating Fields With Gemcitabine and Nab-Paclitaxel for Locally Advanced Pancreatic Adenocarcinoma: Randomized, Open-Label, Pivotal Phase III PANOVA-3 Study
selected_trials.population: 571 patients with unresectable locally advanced pancreatic adenocarcinoma, randomized to TTFields plus gemcitabine/nab-paclitaxel or chemotherapy alone.
selected_trials.intervention: Tumor Treating Fields at 150 kHz, intended for approximately 18 hours/day, with gemcitabine 1,000 mg/m² and nab-paclitaxel 125 mg/m² on days 1, 8 and 15 of 28-day cycles.
selected_trials.comparator: Gemcitabine 1,000 mg/m² plus nab-paclitaxel 125 mg/m² on days 1, 8 and 15 every 28 days.
selected_trials.follow: Peer-reviewed phase III primary report; exact median follow-up and exposure/adherence distributions remain to be transcribed from the full tables.
selected_trials.efficacy: Median OS 16.2 versus 14.2 months (HR 0.82, 95% CI 0.68–0.99; p=0.039). Pain-free survival was 15.2 versus 9.1 months (HR 0.74; p=0.027). The primary report did not show a statistically significant PFS difference.
selected_trials.safety: Grade ≥3 adverse events were reported in approximately 88.6% versus 84.3%; grade 3 device-related skin toxicity was reported in 7.7%. Full event-specific denominators, discontinuation and device adherence require supplement-level reconciliation.
selected_trials.qol: A 2026 secondary quality-of-life analysis is identified as a follow-up publication, but its full domain-level estimates have not been extracted here; no QoL benefit is claimed.
selected_trials.burden: TTFields requires prolonged daily device wear and skin-site care in addition to standard chemotherapy; adherence and treatment interruption are important implementation variables.
selected_trials.limitations: Open-label device trial; modest absolute median OS separation with a confidence interval close to 1.0; device adherence and skin toxicity affect generalizability. No NNT is derived from median OS or HR.
selected_trials.interpretation: The trial reported a statistically significant OS signal for adding TTFields to gemcitabine/nab-paclitaxel in unresectable locally advanced disease. The magnitude, patient burden and applicability should be interpreted alongside device adherence, skin toxicity and the full QoL analysis.

selected_trials.title: Panitumumab vs Bevacizumab Added to Standard First-line Chemotherapy and Overall Survival Among Patients With RAS Wild-type, Left-Sided, Metastatic Colorectal Cancer: A Randomized Clinical Trial
selected_trials.population: 823 patients with RAS wild-type metastatic colorectal cancer; the prespecified left-sided primary population comprised 604 patients. Treatment was mFOLFOX6 plus panitumumab or bevacizumab.
selected_trials.intervention: mFOLFOX6 every 2 weeks plus panitumumab 6 mg/kg IV every 2 weeks.
selected_trials.comparator: mFOLFOX6 every 2 weeks plus bevacizumab 5 mg/kg IV every 2 weeks.
selected_trials.endpoint: Overall survival in patients with left-sided primary tumors.
selected_trials.follow: Long-term analysis; median follow-up approximately 61 months in the primary report.
selected_trials.efficacy: In the left-sided population, median OS was 37.9 versus 34.3 months (HR 0.82, 95.798% CI 0.68–0.99; p=0.03). In the overall RAS wild-type population, median OS was 36.2 versus 31.3 months (HR 0.84; p=0.03). Left-sided PFS was not significantly different; response and R0 resection rates favored panitumumab.
selected_trials.safety: Grade ≥3 adverse events occurred in 71.8% versus 64.9%. Treatment-related deaths were reported in 10 versus 2 patients. Full event-specific safety and discontinuation tables remain to be checked.
selected_trials.qol: No verified patient-reported outcome result is available from the primary report extraction in this run.
selected_trials.burden: Both arms used the same mFOLFOX6 backbone; panitumumab and bevacizumab have distinct dermatologic/electrolyte versus vascular, hypertensive and bleeding risk profiles.
selected_trials.limitations: Open-label design; the OS result is specific to left-sided RAS wild-type disease and should not be extrapolated to right-sided primaries or RAS-mutant disease. No NNT is calculated from median OS/HR alone.
selected_trials.interpretation: PARADIGM supports anti-EGFR therapy as a first-line option for appropriately selected left-sided RAS wild-type metastatic colorectal cancer, with molecular and sidedness selection essential. It does not establish a universal preference across all RAS wild-type disease.

selected_trials.title: Improved Survival with Bevacizumab in Advanced Cervical Cancer
selected_trials.population: 452 patients with metastatic, persistent or recurrent cervical carcinoma and GOG performance status 0–1; patients previously treated with chemotherapy for recurrence were excluded. The chemotherapy-alone and bevacizumab groups contained 225 and 227 patients, respectively.
selected_trials.intervention: Bevacizumab 15 mg/kg IV on day 1 every 21 days added to either cisplatin 50 mg/m² plus paclitaxel 135–175 mg/m², or topotecan 0.75 mg/m² days 1–3 plus paclitaxel 175 mg/m² day 1.
selected_trials.comparator: The same investigator-selected cisplatin/paclitaxel or topotecan/paclitaxel regimens without bevacizumab.
selected_trials.endpoint: Overall survival and adverse events; the primary report assessed OS in the intention-to-treat population.
selected_trials.follow: Final OS analysis included 346 deaths; the later Lancet final analysis reported median OS 16.8 versus 13.3 months.
selected_trials.efficacy: The initial NEJM analysis reported median OS 17.0 versus 13.3 months (HR 0.71, 98% CI 0.54–0.95; p=0.004). The prespecified final analysis reported 16.8 versus 13.3 months (HR 0.77, 95% CI 0.62–0.95; p=0.007).
selected_trials.safety: In the final analysis, fistula of any grade occurred in 15% versus 1% among previously irradiated patients; grade 3 fistula occurred in 6% versus <1%. Grade 3 thromboembolic and hypertensive events also increased with bevacizumab in the original report. Fistula risk is particularly relevant after pelvic RT.
selected_trials.qol: Health-related quality-of-life assessments were collected in the study programme; exact longitudinal domain estimates are not transcribed in this draft.
selected_trials.burden: Three-weekly IV chemotherapy with bevacizumab continued until progression, unacceptable toxicity, withdrawal or complete response. Prior pelvic irradiation is a key safety modifier.
selected_trials.limitations: The trial used two chemotherapy backbones in a factorial design; the bevacizumab effect is pooled across backbones. Fistula risk is concentrated in previously irradiated patients. No NNT is derived from median OS or HR.
selected_trials.interpretation: GOG-240 established a survival benefit from adding bevacizumab to chemotherapy for selected patients with advanced/recurrent cervical cancer, but pelvic irradiation, fistula risk, vascular toxicity and patient selection remain central.
selected_trials.chartTitle: Median overall survival in pooled chemotherapy groups (months; final analysis)

selected_trials.title: Survival with Cemiplimab in Recurrent Cervical Cancer
selected_trials.population: 608 patients with recurrent or metastatic cervical carcinoma progressing after at least one prior systemic therapy for recurrence; squamous, adenocarcinoma and adenosquamous histologies were included.
selected_trials.comparator: Investigator's choice of single-agent chemotherapy: topotecan, vinorelbine, gemcitabine, irinotecan or pemetrexed.
selected_trials.follow: Primary analysis after a median follow-up of approximately 18 months; subsequent biomarker and patient-reported outcome analyses were published separately.
selected_trials.efficacy: Median OS 12.0 versus 8.5 months (HR 0.69, 95% CI 0.56–0.84; p<0.001). Median PFS was 2.8 versus 2.9 months (HR 0.75, 95% CI 0.63–0.89; p<0.001). ORR was 16.4% versus 6.3%. OS benefit was observed in squamous and adenocarcinoma/adenosquamous subgroups.
selected_trials.safety: Grade ≥3 adverse events occurred in 45.0% versus 53.4%; treatment discontinuation for adverse events was approximately 8.7% versus 5.2%. Immune-mediated toxicity requires standard monitoring.
selected_trials.qol: A separate EMPOWER-Cervical-1 patient-reported outcome analysis (NCCN Insights reference 64) reported better patient-reported quality of life, functioning and symptoms with cemiplimab than chemotherapy; exact domain estimates require full PRO-paper extraction.
selected_trials.burden: Fixed-dose IV PD-1 therapy every 3 weeks versus investigator-selected single-agent chemotherapy; treatment exposure and immune-related adverse-event management differ materially.
selected_trials.limitations: Open-label design and a heterogeneous investigator-choice comparator; median PFS was short in both arms despite the OS benefit. No NNT is calculated from median OS/HR.
selected_trials.interpretation: Cemiplimab improved OS after prior systemic therapy for recurrent/metastatic cervical cancer, with benefit reported across histologies. Applicability depends on prior treatment, immune contraindications, regulatory access and current local guideline status.

selected_trials.title: Tisotumab Vedotin as Second- or Third-Line Therapy for Recurrent Cervical Cancer
selected_trials.population: 502 patients with recurrent or metastatic cervical cancer after one or two prior systemic regimens; randomized to tisotumab vedotin or investigator-choice chemotherapy.
selected_trials.intervention: Tisotumab vedotin 2.0 mg/kg IV every 3 weeks, with protocol-directed ocular prophylaxis and monitoring.
selected_trials.comparator: Investigator's choice of topotecan, vinorelbine, gemcitabine, irinotecan or pemetrexed.
selected_trials.follow: Primary phase III analysis; median follow-up approximately 10.8 months at the primary analysis.
selected_trials.efficacy: Median OS 11.5 versus 9.5 months (HR 0.70, 95% CI 0.54–0.89; p=0.004). Median PFS 4.2 versus 2.9 months (HR 0.67, 95% CI 0.54–0.82; p<0.001). ORR 17.8% versus 5.2%.
selected_trials.safety: Grade ≥3 adverse events occurred in approximately 52.0% versus 62.3%. Important ADC-specific risks include ocular toxicity, peripheral neuropathy and bleeding; eye-care prophylaxis/monitoring is integral. Full event-specific and discontinuation tables remain open.
selected_trials.qol: No complete primary QoL/PRO table has been extracted in this run.
selected_trials.burden: Every-3-week ADC infusion with required eye-care measures and monitoring; investigator-choice chemotherapy had regimen-specific schedules.
selected_trials.limitations: Open-label design and heterogeneous chemotherapy comparator; follow-up was relatively short at the primary analysis. The NCCN Insights citation is the 2023 conference abstract (reference 63), not the later NEJM primary paper. No NNT from median survival/HR.
selected_trials.interpretation: Tisotumab vedotin improved OS, PFS and response over investigator-choice chemotherapy in previously treated recurrent/metastatic cervical cancer. Ocular, neurologic and bleeding toxicities and access to prophylactic eye care affect real-world delivery.

selected_trials.setting: Primary advanced or recurrent; first-line systemic therapy
selected_trials.design: Double-blind, placebo-controlled, 1:1 randomized phase III trial with independent dMMR and pMMR cohorts
selected_trials.title: Pembrolizumab plus Chemotherapy in Advanced Endometrial Cancer
selected_trials.population: 816 patients with measurable stage III/IVA, stage IVB or recurrent endometrial cancer. Primary efficacy cohorts included 215 dMMR patients (109 pembrolizumab, 106 placebo) and 550 pMMR patients (276, 274); prior adjuvant chemotherapy was permitted after a treatment-free interval of at least 12 months.
selected_trials.intervention: Pembrolizumab 200 mg IV every 3 weeks with paclitaxel 175 mg/m² and carboplatin AUC 5 for 6 cycles, followed by pembrolizumab 400 mg IV every 6 weeks for up to 14 maintenance cycles.
selected_trials.comparator: Matched placebo with the same paclitaxel/carboplatin chemotherapy and maintenance schedule.
selected_trials.endpoint: Progression-free survival in the dMMR and pMMR cohorts, analyzed separately.
selected_trials.follow: Primary interim PFS analysis; OS and longer-term safety follow-up were immature at publication.
selected_trials.efficacy: At 12 months, dMMR PFS was 74% versus 38% (HR 0.30, 95% CI 0.19–0.48; p<0.001). In pMMR disease, median PFS was 13.1 versus 8.7 months (HR 0.54, 95% CI 0.41–0.71; p<0.001). The dMMR 12-month landmark difference is 36 percentage points; landmark NNT 3 (ceil[1/0.36]).
selected_trials.safety: Grade ≥3 adverse events: dMMR 63.3% (69/109) versus 47.2% (50/106); pMMR 55.1% (152/276) versus 45.3% (124/274). Grade 5 adverse events occurred in 1 versus 2 dMMR patients and 6 versus 2 pMMR patients; attribution differs from all-cause grade ≥3 rates.
selected_trials.qol: A mature patient-reported outcome analysis was not verified in the primary publication used here.
selected_trials.burden: Six 3-weekly chemotherapy cycles followed by up to 14 six-weekly maintenance infusions; immune-mediated toxicity and prolonged treatment duration require consideration.
selected_trials.limitations: Primary endpoint is cohort-specific PFS; OS maturity was limited. NNT is a 12-month Kaplan–Meier landmark estimate for dMMR only, not an overall-trial NNT. Histology and molecular subgroup interpretation remain important.
selected_trials.interpretation: Adding pembrolizumab to carboplatin/paclitaxel improved PFS in both dMMR and pMMR advanced/recurrent endometrial cancer. The largest relative effect was in dMMR disease; toxicity and maintenance burden must be weighed.

selected_trials.design: Double-blind, placebo-controlled, randomized phase III trial
selected_trials.title: Perioperative Nivolumab in Resectable Lung Cancer
selected_trials.population: 461 patients with resectable stage IIA–IIIB NSCLC, including tumors ≥4 cm or node-positive disease; EGFR/ALK-driven tumors were excluded from the key intended population.
selected_trials.intervention: Neoadjuvant nivolumab 360 mg IV every 3 weeks with platinum-doublet chemotherapy for 4 cycles, surgery, then adjuvant nivolumab 480 mg IV every 4 weeks for up to 13 cycles.
selected_trials.comparator: Neoadjuvant placebo with the same platinum-doublet chemotherapy, surgery, then adjuvant placebo.
selected_trials.follow: Primary analysis; 18-month EFS landmark reported. Overall survival remains immature.
selected_trials.efficacy: 18-month EFS was 70.2% versus 50.0% (HR 0.58, 97.36% CI 0.42–0.81; p<0.001). Pathologic complete response was 25.3% versus 4.7%. The 18-month landmark difference is 20.2 percentage points; NNT 5 (ceil[1/0.202]).
selected_trials.safety: Grade 3–4 treatment-related adverse events occurred in 32.5% versus 25.2%. Adjuvant discontinuation and surgical timing require full table-level review; no mature OS benefit is claimed.
selected_trials.qol: Patient-reported outcomes and functional recovery require supplementary table review; no numerical QoL claim is made here.
selected_trials.burden: Four cycles of neoadjuvant chemoimmunotherapy, definitive surgery and up to one year of adjuvant nivolumab; postoperative recovery and immune toxicity may affect treatment completion.
selected_trials.limitations: The primary result is EFS, not mature OS; eligibility and molecular exclusions matter. NNT is an 18-month KM landmark estimate, not a lifetime treatment NNT.
selected_trials.interpretation: Perioperative nivolumab improved EFS and pCR compared with chemotherapy alone in resectable NSCLC. Multidisciplinary surgical fitness, molecular testing and completion of postoperative therapy remain essential.

selected_trials.design: Open-label, randomized, non-inferiority phase III trial
selected_trials.title: Apixaban for the Treatment of Venous Thromboembolism Associated with Cancer
selected_trials.population: 1,170 patients with active cancer and acute symptomatic or incidental proximal DVT or pulmonary embolism; modified intention-to-treat efficacy population included 1,155 patients.
selected_trials.intervention: Apixaban 10 mg orally twice daily for 7 days, then 5 mg twice daily for 6 months.
selected_trials.comparator: Dalteparin 200 IU/kg subcutaneously daily for month 1, then 150 IU/kg daily for months 2–6.
selected_trials.endpoint: Recurrent venous thromboembolism during the 6-month treatment period; major bleeding was the principal safety endpoint.
selected_trials.efficacy: Recurrent VTE occurred in 5.6% versus 7.9% (HR 0.63, 95% CI 0.37–1.07); apixaban met non-inferiority (p<0.001). Superiority was not demonstrated (p≈0.09). Major bleeding was 3.8% versus 4.0%.
selected_trials.safety: Major bleeding occurred in 22/576 (3.8%) versus 23/579 (4.0%); no excess major bleeding was observed with apixaban. Clinically relevant non-major bleeding and cancer-site subgroup analyses require full supplement review.
selected_trials.qol: No validated QoL endpoint was verified in the primary trial report.
selected_trials.burden: Oral twice-daily treatment avoids daily injections; drug–drug interactions, renal function, gastrointestinal/genitourinary lesions and adherence remain important.
selected_trials.limitations: The primary hypothesis was non-inferiority. The numerically lower recurrence rate does not establish superiority; therefore no NNT is calculated. GI/GU bleeding risk and active mucosal lesions may change agent choice.
selected_trials.interpretation: Apixaban was non-inferior to dalteparin for cancer-associated VTE with similar major bleeding in CARAVAGGIO. The result should not be interpreted as proven superior efficacy; individualized bleeding-risk assessment remains essential.

selected_trials.design: Double-blind, randomized, non-inferiority phase III trial
selected_trials.title: Extended Reduced-Dose Apixaban for Cancer-Associated Venous Thromboembolism
selected_trials.population: 1,766 patients with active cancer and proximal DVT or pulmonary embolism who had completed at least 6 months of anticoagulation and were considered to require extended treatment.
selected_trials.intervention: Apixaban 2.5 mg orally twice daily for 12 months.
selected_trials.comparator: Apixaban 5 mg orally twice daily for 12 months.
selected_trials.endpoint: Recurrent VTE during the 12-month extended-treatment period; clinically relevant bleeding was a key secondary safety endpoint.
selected_trials.follow: Median follow-up approximately 11.8 months during extended treatment.
selected_trials.efficacy: Recurrent VTE occurred in 2.1% versus 2.8% (adjusted sub-HR 0.76, 95% CI 0.41–1.41; p=0.001 for non-inferiority). Clinically relevant bleeding occurred in 12.1% versus 15.6% (sub-HR 0.75, 95% CI 0.58–0.97; p=0.03).
selected_trials.safety: The reduced-dose strategy lowered clinically relevant bleeding; major bleeding was also numerically lower. Full grade 3–5 event and subgroup tables remain to be reconciled before release.
selected_trials.qol: No QoL result was verified in the primary report.
selected_trials.burden: Twice-daily oral therapy for a further 12 months; dose reduction is relevant to long-term bleeding burden after the initial therapeutic phase.
selected_trials.limitations: This is an extended-treatment population after at least 6 months of anticoagulation, not an acute VTE trial. The primary result is non-inferiority for recurrence; NNT is calculated only for the secondary clinically relevant bleeding reduction at 12 months.
selected_trials.interpretation: API-CAT supports reduced-dose apixaban as a non-inferior extended-treatment option in selected patients with active cancer, with less clinically relevant bleeding than full-dose apixaban. It should not be extrapolated to initial acute treatment.

selected_trials.setting: Acute cancer-associated VTE; 6–12 months of anticoagulation
selected_trials.design: Open-label, randomized, non-inferiority phase III trial
selected_trials.title: Edoxaban for the Treatment of Cancer-Associated Venous Thromboembolism
selected_trials.population: 1,050 patients randomized; modified intention-to-treat efficacy population 1,046 patients with active cancer and acute symptomatic or incidental VTE.
selected_trials.intervention: Edoxaban 60 mg orally once daily after at least 5 days of parenteral anticoagulation; dose reduced to 30 mg for low body weight, creatinine clearance 30–50 mL/min or selected P-glycoprotein inhibitors.
selected_trials.comparator: Dalteparin 200 IU/kg subcutaneously daily for month 1, then 150 IU/kg daily for months 2–12.
selected_trials.endpoint: Composite of recurrent VTE or major bleeding over 6–12 months; recurrent VTE and major bleeding were separately assessed.
selected_trials.follow: Treatment duration 6–12 months; primary outcome assessed through the treatment period.
selected_trials.efficacy: The composite outcome occurred in 12.8% versus 13.5% (HR 0.97, 95% CI 0.70–1.36; non-inferiority p=0.006). Recurrent VTE was 7.9% versus 11.3%; superiority was not established for the composite.
selected_trials.safety: Major bleeding occurred in 6.9% versus 4.0%, an absolute increase of 2.9 percentage points (95% CI for difference approximately 0.1–5.6). Point-estimate NNH 35 (ceil[1/0.029]); excess bleeding was concentrated in gastrointestinal cancer.
selected_trials.qol: No QoL result was verified in the primary report.
selected_trials.burden: Oral once-daily edoxaban follows an initial parenteral anticoagulant lead-in; dose reduction criteria and GI mucosal bleeding risk are clinically important.
selected_trials.limitations: Non-inferiority design; recurrent VTE reduction should not be interpreted as proven superiority. The NNH is a point estimate for major bleeding over the trial treatment period; confidence limits are wide.
selected_trials.interpretation: Edoxaban was non-inferior to dalteparin for the composite endpoint but increased major bleeding, particularly in GI cancer. The bleeding signal is central to agent selection in luminal GI malignancy.

selected_trials.setting: Resectable macroscopic stage III; neoadjuvant response-adapted strategy
selected_trials.title: Neoadjuvant Ipilimumab and Nivolumab in Resectable Stage III Melanoma
selected_trials.population: 423 patients with resectable macroscopic stage III melanoma and clinically detectable nodal disease; randomized to neoadjuvant immunotherapy or surgery followed by adjuvant nivolumab.
selected_trials.intervention: Two neoadjuvant cycles of ipilimumab 1 mg/kg plus nivolumab 3 mg/kg every 3 weeks, followed by surgery. Postoperative systemic treatment was response-adapted; patients with major pathological response generally omitted adjuvant therapy, while non-MPR patients received adjuvant treatment according to protocol and BRAF status.
selected_trials.comparator: Immediate surgery followed by adjuvant nivolumab 480 mg IV every 4 weeks for up to 12 cycles.
selected_trials.follow: Primary analysis with median follow-up approximately 9.9 months; long-term EFS/OS maturity remains limited.
selected_trials.efficacy: 12-month EFS was 83.7% versus 57.2% (HR 0.32, 99.9% CI 0.15–0.66; p<0.001). Major pathological response was approximately 59% in the neoadjuvant arm. The 12-month landmark difference is 26.5 percentage points; NNT 4 (ceil[1/0.265]).
selected_trials.safety: Grade ≥3 treatment-related adverse events occurred in 29.7% versus 14.7%. Immune-related toxicity and timing of surgery are important; full perioperative complication and treatment-completion tables remain open.
selected_trials.qol: No mature QoL/PRO result was verified in the primary report.
selected_trials.burden: Two preoperative combination-immunotherapy cycles followed by surgery and response-directed postoperative therapy; toxicity may delay or alter surgery and postoperative treatment.
selected_trials.limitations: Short primary follow-up, response-adapted postoperative treatment and stage III-only population. NNT is a 12-month KM landmark estimate. The accessible NCCN Melanoma Insights Version 2.2024 predates this primary report and does not cite NADINA.
selected_trials.interpretation: NADINA supports neoadjuvant ipilimumab/nivolumab with response-directed postoperative therapy in resectable macroscopic stage III melanoma. Longer follow-up and careful toxicity/surgical planning remain essential.

selected_trials.setting: Resectable stage IIIB–IVC; neoadjuvant-adjuvant versus adjuvant-only pembrolizumab
selected_trials.title: Neoadjuvant–Adjuvant or Adjuvant-Only Pembrolizumab in Advanced Melanoma
selected_trials.population: 313 patients with clinically detectable, resectable stage IIIB–IVC melanoma; 154 assigned to neoadjuvant-adjuvant pembrolizumab and 159 to adjuvant-only pembrolizumab.
selected_trials.intervention: Pembrolizumab 200 mg IV every 3 weeks for 3 preoperative doses, surgery, then 15 additional adjuvant doses.
selected_trials.comparator: Surgery followed by 18 doses of adjuvant pembrolizumab 200 mg IV every 3 weeks.
selected_trials.follow: Primary analysis with median follow-up 14.7 months; 2-year EFS landmark reported.
selected_trials.efficacy: Two-year EFS was 72% versus 49% (p=0.004; HR approximately 0.58, 95% CI 0.39–0.87). The 23-percentage-point landmark difference gives NNT 5 (ceil[1/0.23]).
selected_trials.safety: Grade ≥3 treatment-related adverse events occurred in 12% versus 14%. Surgery-related events and delays should be considered with preoperative immunotherapy.
selected_trials.qol: No mature QoL/PRO estimate was verified in the primary report.
selected_trials.burden: Three preoperative infusions before surgery and 15 postoperative doses versus surgery followed by 18 doses; neoadjuvant therapy changes the timing of systemic treatment.
selected_trials.limitations: Phase II and relatively short follow-up at the primary analysis; EFS is not OS. NNT is a 2-year KM landmark estimate.
selected_trials.interpretation: SWOG S1801 established a randomized EFS signal for neoadjuvant-adjuvant pembrolizumab over adjuvant-only therapy in resectable high-risk melanoma. It supports sequencing rather than proving a survival advantage.

nnt.event: Event or death by 24 months (complement of published KM EFS estimate)
nnt.note: Landmark NNT from the published 2-year KM EFS rates.

selected_trials.setting: Progression within 6 months of platinum; second-line or later
selected_trials.design: Open-label, randomized phase III trial with investigator-selected chemotherapy backbone
selected_trials.title: Bevacizumab Combined With Chemotherapy for Platinum-Resistant Recurrent Ovarian Cancer: The AURELIA Open-Label Randomized Phase III Trial
selected_trials.population: 361 patients with platinum-resistant recurrent ovarian, fallopian tube or primary peritoneal carcinoma; progression within 6 months of platinum. Investigator selected weekly paclitaxel, pegylated liposomal doxorubicin or topotecan before randomization.
selected_trials.intervention: Selected chemotherapy plus bevacizumab 10 mg/kg IV every 2 weeks or 15 mg/kg every 3 weeks, according to chemotherapy schedule.
selected_trials.follow: Primary PFS analysis after 301 PFS events; OS follow-up continued.
selected_trials.efficacy: Median PFS 6.7 versus 3.4 months (HR 0.48, 95% CI 0.38–0.60; p<0.001). ORR was 27.3% versus 11.8% (p=0.001). Median OS was 16.6 versus 13.3 months (HR 0.85, 95% CI 0.66–1.08; p=0.174).
selected_trials.safety: Grade ≥3 hypertension occurred in approximately 7% versus 1%; GI perforation occurred in 2.2% of bevacizumab-treated patients and none in chemotherapy alone. Grade ≥2 hypertension and proteinuria were more common with bevacizumab.
selected_trials.qol: The AURELIA patient-reported outcome analysis reported improvement in abdominal/GI symptoms for some patients receiving bevacizumab-containing therapy; full domain-level estimates and denominators remain to be extracted.
selected_trials.burden: Treatment burden depends on the selected chemotherapy backbone; bevacizumab adds repeated IV infusions and monitoring for hypertension, proteinuria, bleeding and GI perforation.
selected_trials.limitations: Open-label design and investigator-selected chemotherapy; OS was not statistically significant. No NNT is derived from median PFS/OS or HR.
selected_trials.interpretation: AURELIA demonstrated improved PFS and response with bevacizumab plus chemotherapy in selected platinum-resistant ovarian cancer, without a statistically significant OS improvement. Bowel involvement, obstruction and perforation risk are critical selection factors.

selected_trials.setting: First platinum-sensitive relapse; secondary cytoreductive surgery
selected_trials.title: Randomized Trial of Cytoreductive Surgery for Relapsed Ovarian Cancer
selected_trials.population: 407 patients at first platinum-sensitive relapse after ≥6 months, selected by a positive AGO score: ECOG 0, ascites ≤500 mL and complete resection at primary surgery; disease considered amenable to secondary cytoreduction.
selected_trials.intervention: Secondary cytoreductive surgery followed by platinum-based chemotherapy.
selected_trials.comparator: Platinum-based chemotherapy without secondary cytoreductive surgery.
selected_trials.follow: Primary analysis; median follow-up approximately 35 months.
selected_trials.efficacy: Median OS 53.7 versus 46.0 months (HR 0.75, 95% CI 0.59–0.96; p=0.02). Median PFS was 18.4 versus 14.0 months (HR 0.66, 95% CI 0.54–0.82; p<0.001). Complete resection was achieved in approximately 75.5% of patients who underwent surgery.
selected_trials.safety: No perioperative mortality within 30 days was reported; grade ≥3 surgical and systemic toxicity tables require full supplement-level review. Operative morbidity depends on disease distribution and centre experience.
selected_trials.qol: Quality of life was not worsened by surgery at the reported 6- and 12-month assessments; complete domain-level values remain to be extracted.
selected_trials.burden: The surgical strategy adds a major operation before platinum-based chemotherapy; benefit depends strongly on the ability to achieve complete gross resection.
selected_trials.limitations: Highly selected AGO-positive population; results should not be extrapolated to patients with poor performance status, ascites >500 mL or incomplete primary resection. No NNT from median OS/PFS alone.
selected_trials.interpretation: DESKTOP III supports secondary cytoreduction followed by platinum chemotherapy in carefully selected patients with platinum-sensitive first relapse when complete resection is achievable. Selection and surgical expertise are integral to the result.

selected_trials.setting: Interval cytoreductive surgery after neoadjuvant chemotherapy
selected_trials.title: Hyperthermic Intraperitoneal Chemotherapy in Ovarian Cancer
selected_trials.population: 245 patients with stage III epithelial ovarian cancer without progression after at least three cycles of neoadjuvant carboplatin/paclitaxel and considered suitable for interval cytoreductive surgery.
selected_trials.intervention: Interval cytoreductive surgery plus HIPEC with cisplatin 100 mg/m² heated intraperitoneally for approximately 90 minutes; detailed perfusion temperature, carrier and sodium-thiosulfate nephroprotection protocol require protocol/supplement recheck.
selected_trials.follow: Primary analysis at median follow-up approximately 4.7 years; a later long-term analysis at approximately 10 years is linked as follow-up.
selected_trials.efficacy: Median RFS 14.2 versus 10.7 months (HR 0.66, 95% CI 0.50–0.87; p=0.003). Median OS 45.7 versus 33.9 months (HR 0.67, 95% CI 0.48–0.94; p=0.02). The long-term follow-up reported persistent RFS/OS separation; exact table-level estimates remain to be reconciled.
selected_trials.safety: Grade 3–4 adverse events were approximately 25% versus 27% (p=0.76) in the primary report. Renal toxicity, postoperative morbidity and perfusion protocol details require full supplement review.
selected_trials.qol: No verified patient-reported QoL result is available from the primary report extraction in this run.
selected_trials.burden: HIPEC adds a 90-minute heated intraperitoneal cisplatin procedure to interval surgery and requires anaesthetic, renal-protection and specialist perfusion infrastructure.
selected_trials.limitations: The trial applies to selected stage III patients responding to neoadjuvant chemotherapy and undergoing interval surgery; it does not establish a role for HIPEC at primary debulking or in all ovarian cancer. No NNT from median RFS/OS alone.
selected_trials.interpretation: OVHIPEC-1 reported improved RFS and OS with cisplatin HIPEC at interval cytoreduction in a selected stage III population. Reproducibility depends on patient selection, complete cytoreduction, surgical expertise and protocol-level renal protection.
